messages:
matt: Heads-up — I've been seeing a slow, steady rise in single-bit ECC on a subset of cards in us-west-2 over the past 10 days. Not big spikes, more like a background leak that increments every few hours.

alexa: Can you paste the query you used? sounds like wearout vs transient.

matt: Sure — started with this to spot accumulation across a week:
```promql
sum by(card_uuid) (increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_count[7d]))
```
shows ~80-200 on 4 cards, whereas most cards are <5.

sara: yikes. That will eventually lead to uncorrectable errors. We should avoid immediate nodal drains for a single alert — too noisy — but we need a policy for slow accumulation.

jin: Agree. Proposal: add a long-window "wearout" alert that triggers a maintenance workflow when a card crosses a cumulative threshold, separate from the short-term DCGM spike alerts.

alexa: +1. Something like:
```promql
avg_over_time(increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_count[7d])[7d:1d]) > 50
```
But that's messy. Better: two rules — a recording rule for weekly_increase and an alert rule that fires if weekly_increase > 75 for 3 consecutive evaluations.

matt: Draft recording rule (names intentionally explicit):
```yaml
- record: gpu:dcgm:ecc_singlebit:7d_increase
  expr: sum by(job, instance, card_uuid) (increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_count[7d]))
```
Alert rule idea:
```yaml
- alert: GPUCardWearout
  expr: gpu:dcgm:ecc_singlebit:7d_increase > 75
  for: 72h
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Card {{ $labels.card_uuid }} showing sustained ECC single-bit accumulation"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-wearout"
```
This gives 3 days of sustained accumulation before paging.

sara: I like the multi-day gate. Also recommend keeping a secondary metric: rate of corrected ECCs turning into uncorrectable XIDs. So correlate dcgm_xid_error_count increases within 30d window. If both rise, escalate faster.

jin: For operator flow, suggested runbook steps in the annotation: 
- label node: `kubectl label node <node> gpu.rma-needed=true`
- cordon & drain non-critical pods (use fleetctl to preserve reserved capacity)
- run hardware stress test: `gpu-healthcheck --stress --duration 2h --card <id>`
- if failures reproduce, open RMA ticket and mark as degraded in inventory.

alexa: We should also provide a low-friction soft-action for platform teams: auto-add the node to a maintenance pool (no immediate drain) to collect more telemetry and reduce impact to running jobs.

matt: Right — plan: soft label + 7d recheck. Hard action (drain + RMA) after either: weekly_increase > 200 or weekly_increase > 75 AND xid_uncorrectable_rate_in_30d > 1.

infra-bot: [alert] GPUCardWearout fired for card_uuid=abcd-ef12 on node gpunode-usw2-17 — weekly_increase=129. Scheduling 72h re-eval.

sara: For Prometheus tuning — set recording rules to evaluate every 1h and alerts every 6h with `for: 72h`. That reduces flapping and reduces alert noise compared to per-5m rules.

jin: Test plan: 
- Inject synthetic metric into staging exporter with the same label set and validate that the alert records but does not page until 72h.
- Run canary on a small subset of nodes (us-west-2a) for 2 weeks.

alexa: Also add dashboard tiles: 7d increase heatmap by rack, and a timeline that overlays weekly_increase with dcgm_xid_uncorrectable_count. Helps triage quickly.

matt: Operational impact: if we mark ~4 cards across region for RMA over next month, capacity loss is ~1.5% in worst case. We should coordinate with capacity planning to pre-provision spare nodes for critical pools.

sara: Agreed — I'll sync with capacity and paste plan here. Also propose a short-lived label `gpu.wearout_watch=true` so autoscaler can avoid packing extra low-priority jobs on those nodes.

jin: One more: for existing historical noise, add a suppression window in Alertmanager to avoid re-alerting the same card within 14 days unless severity increases. Keep the alert history for evaluation.

matt: I'll open a PR with the recording + alert rules and an entry in the runbooks repo. Targeting canary rollout Monday.

alexa: Thanks — please tag @oncall in the PR and link the staging experiment. :thumbsup:

matt: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/prometheus/commit/ab12c3 (draft) — includes rule, dashboard JSON, and runbook stub.

infra-bot: [info] Scheduled canary rollout of GPUCardWearout rules to staging cluster at 2029-05-01T04:00Z.

sara: Nice. After canary let's reconvene and set final thresholds based on false positive rate.

jin: 👍 If anyone wants to pair on the stress test harness, ping me.

alexa: moving to implement. closing loop in two weeks. :white_check_mark:
